words: I'll never forget the time I went two weeks without Instagram while travelling.
By day three, I was reading books again.
By day seven, I was having conversations I'd remember.
One of the key things I realised is that the technology we think we need is often the thing standing between us and the life we actually want.

words: What makes the biggest difference, in my experience, is routine.
One of the key things I've learned is that eating proper meals instead of relying on snacks saves both time and energy — and your brain, it turns out, works considerably better when it's been fed.
If you often skip breakfast, try preparing something simple the night before.
It sounds obvious, but for most students it's genuinely transformative.

words: For me personally, the best thing about imagining a world without social media is the mental space it would create.
What makes it so concerning is how these platforms were designed to keep us scrolling — not to make us happier.
Apart from the obvious distractions, another thing that really stands out is how they reshape the way we see ourselves, always comparing our private reality to someone else's curated highlight reel.

words: As far as I'm concerned, being famous for scientific discovery would be the greatest achievement imaginable.
One of the key things I love about science is how a single idea can change millions of lives — often long after the person who had it is gone.
If I had to choose one example, it would be someone like Marie Curie, celebrated not for fame itself, but for what she gave the world.

words: For me personally, the best thing about Sintra is how it manages to feel both grand and intimate at the same time.
You can wander through royal gardens, stumble upon hidden chapels, and stop at a small café for a warm pastry, all within an hour.
Apart from its beauty, another thing that really stands out is how accessible it is — just forty minutes by train from Lisbon.
